keyframe_review.note: Not a Confederation shape. Cliopatria's 170,588 km2 outline holds Berlin, Breslau, Stettin, Königsberg and Tilsit (gazetteer check: 516 cells in Poland, 142 in Germany, 61 in Russia) and has no cell in common with Bavaria, Saxony or Westphalia: it is the Prussian rump of 1807-1813, and the page says 'Prussia itself was not a member'. The confederation's own land is its members' (the union given; new keyframes 1806-1810 above, 1811-1813 below); the infobox 325,700 km2 is the whole peak, against Cliopatria's 170,588 km2 (ratio 1.9). The Prussian group must claim this shape (Cliopatria's Prussia has no 1809-1813 row).

keyframe_review.note: The confederation ended in 1813: 'The allies opposing Napoleon dissolved the Confederation of the Rhine on 4 November 1813' and 'On 30 May 1814, the Treaty of Paris declared the German states independent'. Cliopatria's 1814 shape (258,129 km2) holds Berlin, Cologne, Münster, Magdeburg, Leipzig, Kassel and Hannover: Prussia and the lands it held in 1814, not the confederation. Draw nothing for the confederation in 1814.

ledger.note: 12 July 1806: German princes found the Confederation of the Rhine in Napoleon's protectorate. The member table dates the co-founders 'Jul 1806' (Baden, Bavaria, Berg, Hesse-Darmstadt, Württemberg, Regensburg, Arenberg, Hohenzollern-Hechingen and -Sigmaringen, Isenburg, Leyen, Liechtenstein, Nassau, Salm); 'On 12 July, the Paris envoys of the various princes were summoned to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs'. An association, not territory.

notes:
TYPE. Filed as umbrella: an association of sovereign states under Napoleon's protection, whose members each have their own dossier (rule 4: associations are never territory). The 'gain' events record the dated accession of each member and are not land changes; the keyframes give the union of the members' Cliopatria shapes only as the extent a state page may quote. If the colour/render rules want a drawn Confederation, use those unions.

CLIOPATRIA ROWS ARE PRUSSIA'S. The two Cliopatria shapes (1809-1813, 1814) are not the confederation. The 1809-1813 shape holds Berlin, Breslau, Stettin, Königsberg and Tilsit and shares no cell with Bavaria, Saxony or Westphalia (gazetteer check); the 1814 shape holds Berlin, Cologne, Münster, Magdeburg, Leipzig, Kassel and Hannover. Cliopatria's Kingdom of Prussia has no shape for 1807-1813 (only a 1,787 km2 strip in 1807-1808) and a 87 km2 sliver in 1814, so these two rows appear to carry the Prussian territory under the wrong name. The page says 'Prussia itself was not a member'. The Prussia group (eu-09) should take the 1809-1814 shapes; this is the strongest finding of this dossier.

NOT SETTLED. (1) The page names 'the Free Hansa towns of Hamburg, Lübeck, and Bremen' among the German lands 'not included in the Confederation' (with Austria, Prussia, Danish Holstein and Swedish Pomerania; reviewer eu-20-h, 2026-11-01), so Lübeck and Bremen are rightly left out of the unions. (2) The minor founders without a Cliopatria shape: Arenberg, Isenburg, Leyen, Liechtenstein, Salm, Hohenzollern-Hechingen, Schaumburg-Lippe, Schwarzburg, Saxe-Coburg, Saxe-Meiningen. (3) Month of the founding: 12 July 1806 (narrative), 'Jul 1806' (table). (4) Frankfurt as capital is the infobox's; the Grand Duchy of Frankfurt (1810) has no Cliopatria row. (5) The page's 325,700 km2 has no year.

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: Grand Duchy of Frankfurt (1810-1813), Principality of Schaumburg-Lippe, Saxe-Hildburghausen, and the minor mediatised founders (Arenberg has a dossier; Salm, Isenburg, Leyen, Liechtenstein, Hohenzollern-Hechingen do not).
